traceability.notes: All of the acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md are implemented and verified: - Core Functionality: Every relevant rule (require-story-annotation, require-req-annotation, require-branch-annotation, valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, valid-req-reference) exposes specific, actionable messages via meta.messages and uses context.report with well-structured data objects instead of generic failures. - Quality & Integration: Messages follow ESLint best practices (messageId + template with {{placeholders}}, data fields, hasSuggestions for autofix cases) and are integrated into the plugin’s configs via TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES and createTraceabilityFlatConfig. Tests use RuleTester and direct listener invocation to verify rule behavior under ESLint-like conditions. - User Experience: Error messages clearly identify what is wrong (missing @story/@req, invalid formats, missing files, invalid paths, missing requirements), where (function/branch/comment node, functionName, storyPath/reqId in data), and how to fix it (explicit suggestions and autofixers or example paths/IDs in the text). The dedicated error-reporting.test.ts suite checks the precise content and suggestion wiring for require-story-annotation. - Error Handling: valid-story-reference and its utilities distinguish missing files from filesystem errors, emitting fileMissing vs fileAccessError with contextual error strings; tests simulate EACCES/EIO errors and confirm that no uncaught exceptions occur. Annotation-format and deep validation rules handle invalid configuration and path traversal safely, reporting clear diagnostics. - Documentation & Consistency: The story’s conventions ({{functionName}}, {{missing}}, {{details}}, {{filePath}}/storyPath/reqId, severity mapping) are reflected in the implemented messages and the JSDoc annotations across rule and helper files. Multiple test files explicitly tag this story and its REQ-ERROR-* requirements, providing strong traceability. Given this concrete implementation and passing tests, the story 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING is fully implemented and is assessed as PASSED.
